newsOutletDelayDays.citation: Days until a local outlet's report reaches someone who follows politics most of the time (engagement 1) and trusts the media as much as the average adult: the next day. Someone who follows less, or trusts the media less, hears later in proportion (delay = this / (engagement x trust / average trust)). The proportion is an assumption checked by how fast results spread. Spread 0.5 to 2. Research, October 12, 2026 (data/research/stand-in-figures-2026-10-12.json): GAME ASSUMPTION kept; no measured counterpart (the repository's R20 research cannot justify stories per event or word-of-mouth speed). The audience side is bounded by Pew Research Center (2024), Attention to local news: 22% of adults follow local news very closely (9% of ages 18-29, 35% of ages 65 and over).

newsMaxAgeDays.citation: Days a story stays news: after this no outlet or conversation carries it, so people whose habits would bring it later never hear it. Spread 14 to 60.
